title: Steady-State Operations and Cost Optimization Playbook for Private Deployments
author: Maya Chen
content:
Overview

Purpose
This playbook codifies best-practices for running Redwood Private deployments in steady-state (week-to-week operations) while minimizing unit cost and preserving latency SLOs. It targets engineering runbooks for platform and customer-facing SREs who manage: VPC-based private control planes, on-prem clusters, and hybrid (cloud + private) topologies.

Scope
- Day-to-day capacity adjustments, cost control levers, and chargeback signals.
- Safe short-term remedies for cost spikes and guidance for longer-term resourcing changes.
- Integrations: Redwood control plane, redwoodctl, customer metrics exporters (Prometheus), and alerting (PagerDuty).
- Not covered: initial provisioning (see deployment-readiness checklist), or deep kernel/runtime optimization (see serving-runtime docs).

Key Objectives and KPIs
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile tail <= configured SLO (default: 180ms for generation workloads, 60ms for embeddings).
- Cost per 1K tokens: track and reduce month-over-month by >5% through batching/caching adjustments.
- Capacity efficiency: average GPU utilization 40–70% during business hours; burst headroom >= 20% for 99% of 1h windows.
- Incident goal: mitigate customer-impacting capacity incidents to restore service within 30 minutes for standard severity.

Ownership and Routines
- Primary oncall: Private Deployments SRE (pager on rotation).
- Capacity planning owner: Capacity Planning team (engineering).
- Monthly cadence: 1) Capacity review, 2) Cost reconciliation, 3) Prometheus alert tuning.

Operational Controls (Quick Reference)
- Autoscaling policy: prefer horizontal pod scaling for user-level frontends; prefer controlled vertical scaling for model-serving nodes for predictable costs.
- Prefix/KV cache retention: set default TTL 5m, extend to 30m for steady prompt-heavy workloads with caching savings.
- Model downgrade policy: automatic fallback to a lower-cost quantized variant when queue length exceeds threshold 50 for >2m.
- Emergency fallback: route non-sensitive workloads to Redwood Hosted API (requires customer consent and configured route policy).

Configuration Table: Suggested steady-state profile (single-zone private deployment)
| Component | Suggested baseline | Rationale/Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Model-serving GPU type | A5000 / equivalent | Good balance of memory and throughput for mainstream models |
| Serving nodes per 100 qps (gen) | 3–4 | Empirical baseline — validate with perf suite |
| Disk (OS + logs) | 500GB NVMe | Fast local disk for cache and logs (rotate daily) |
| Network | 25Gbps inter-node | Reduces KV/cache synchronization tail latencies |
| KV cache memory | 16–64GB per node | Depends on workload; monitor cache hit ratio |
| Snapshot frequency | 15m for model-weights index | Short snapshots reduce warm-up time after restarts |
| Backup retention | 30 days (cold), 7 days (hot) | Meet recovery and compliance needs |
| KMS rotation | 90 days | Align with corporate key policies |

(Use this table as a starting point and adapt per customer SLA and model mix.)

Signals and Alerts (must-haves)
- Cost signals:
  1) Unexpected increase in chargeable GPU-hours > 20% relative to rolling-7d baseline.
  2) Monthly committed capacity burn rate slipping > 10% vs forecast.
- Performance signals:
  1) P95 generation latency above SLO for 15m window.
  2) Retry rate > 2% over 10m window.
  3) Queue depth per node > 75% of capacity for 5m.
- Health signals:
  1) Node OOMs / CUDA memory errors spike.
  2) Heartbeat missing from control-plane agents for > 2m.

Playbooks (Procedures)
1) Cost spike detected (alert: GPU-hours up >20%)
   1. Triage: check running jobs (redwoodctl admin list-jobs --since 1h).
   2. Identify cause: sudden traffic surge? long-running evals? misconfigured test traffic?
   3. Short-term mitigation (within 10 minutes):
      - If traffic surge, enable rate-limiting policy for non-critical routes: redwoodctl policy set --route /embed --rate 1000r/m --scope customer.
      - If evals are running on production, move to isolated dedicated capacity: redwoodctl admin migrate-job --job-id <id> --target dedicated-queue.
      - If model causing high token cost, flip to quantized variant: redwoodctl model set-active --model-id <low-cost-variant> --route /generate --grace 30s.
   4. Medium-term: schedule capacity increase or customer throttle changes in next maintenance window; update cost forecast.
   5. Post-incident: run cost root-cause analysis, update alert thresholds to reduce false positives.

2) Sustained queue growth and tail latency regression
   1. Check autoscaler status: kubectl get hpa -n redwood | grep model-serving.
   2. If HPA is saturated, increase target CPU/GPU utilization threshold (example: kubectl patch hpa/model-serving -p '{"spec":{"targetCPUUtilizationPercentage":70}}').
   3. If vertical limits hit (OOM/CUDA errors), temporarily spin up compensatory nodes: redwoodctl cluster scale --replicas +2 --node-type a5000-temporary --ttl 4h.
   4. Enable request batching for low-latency tolerant routes: update route configuration to batchingMode=windowed, batchWindowMs=10.
   5. If issue persists >30m, trigger model downgrade fallback and notify customer success.

3) Control-plane heartbeat loss (partial network isolation)
   1. Confirm failure: check agent logs (journalctl -u redwood-agent) and network routes (ip route).
   2. If only control-plane unreachable but node-level inference still healthy: set a maintenance flag to avoid automated scale-down: redwoodctl maintenance start --reason "control-plane-unreachable" --ttl 2h.
   3. If nodes show degraded inference, failover to fallback region or hosted API if configured.

Upgrade and Rollback Considerations (steady-state oriented)
- Upgrade windows: prefer off-peak local times (customer-defined) with a default 2h maintenance window.
- Canary policy: 5% traffic -> 20% -> 50% -> 100% with 15m observation windows and automated rollback on error budget exhaustion (>1% error or P95 breach).
- Safe rollback checklist:
  - Confirm existing snapshot availability and last successful schema migration time.
  - Pause automated job-schedulers and throttle non-critical traffic.
  - Revert model-serving images and config: redwoodctl deploy rollback --entire-release --to-revision <rev>.
  - Monitor P95 and error rates for 30m post-rollback.

Cost Optimization Levers (practical guidance)
- Quantization Profiles: maintain a small catalog of production-verified quantized variants. Use telemetry to suggest candidates: if per-token cost > baseline by 15%, run automatic A/B evaluations.
- Batching: tune batchWindowMs and maxBatchSize per-route. Avoid overly large windows that increase latency for tail-sensitive routes.
- Prefix/KV caching: prefer larger TTLs for cold-start-heavy workloads. Monitor cache hit ratio; target >60% for cache-backed workloads.
- Spot/Preemptible Planning: where acceptable, run non-critical workloads (evaluation, retraining) on spot instances with 2-minute graceful eviction handlers.
- Idle capacity reclamation: detect nodes idle > 4h and run scale-down policies; require drift-approval for nodes with pinned model caches.

Observability and Dashboards
- Essential dashboards:
  1) Cost by tenant / model / route (daily and 30-day trend).
  2) Latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) by model and route.
  3) Cache hit ratio and KV telemetry.
  4) GPU utilization heatmap across zones.
- Exporters: ensure node_exporter, nvidia-smi exporter, and redwoodctl-prometheus are present. Key metrics to expose: redwood_inference_queue_depth, redwood_model_batch_size, redwood_cache_hit_ratio, node_gpu_free_memory.

Customer Communication Templates (when cost causes changes)
- Short (incident): "We observed elevated inference costs caused by a surge in token volume. We applied a temporary throttle and flipped lower-cost model variants to maintain SLOs. We will follow up with costs and mitigation steps by EOD."
- Post-incident (detailed): include timeline, root cause, mitigations applied, and recommended long-term changes (e.g., reserved capacity, route-level rate limits).

Runbook Appendix: Useful Commands
- Check running inference jobs: redwoodctl admin list-jobs --format table --since 60m
- Migrate job to dedicated queue: redwoodctl admin migrate-job --job-id <id> --target dedicated-queue
- Scale cluster temporarily: redwoodctl cluster scale --replicas +2 --node-type a5000-temp --ttl 4h
- Force model-variant swap: redwoodctl model set-active --model-id <low-cost-variant> --route /generate --grace 30s
- Start maintenance to avoid automated scale-downs: redwoodctl maintenance start --reason "investigation" --ttl 2h

Postmortem and Continuous Improvement
- For every cost or capacity incident, produce a 1-page postmortem within 5 business days that includes: impact, timeline, root cause, contributing factors, action items with owners and due dates.
- Quarterly optimizations: run a cost-savings sprint focusing on right-sizing, cache tuning, and evaluating new quantization profiles.

Appendix: Sample Terraform snippet for ephemeral capacity overlay
```hcl
# Overlay module to add temporary GPU nodes for surge capacity
module "temp_gpu_spike" {
  source = "git::ssh://git@repo/internal/terraform/modules/temp-gpu-overlay.git"
  cluster_id = var.cluster_id
  node_count = var.temp_node_count
  node_type  = "a5000-temp"
  ttl_hours  = 4
}
```
